usefulness.use_case: Algorithmic Efficiency Screening in Quantitative & Tech Interviews
usefulness.example: Evaluates whether candidates discover the O(N) two-pointer technique on sorted arrays versus naive O(N^2) brute-force nested loops across 10,000+ elements.
usefulness.benefit: Automates algorithmic performance gating without subjective manual code reviews.

usefulness.example: When an array contains multiple valid index pairs (e.g. arr[1]+arr[4]=70 and arr[2]+arr[3]=70), the agent accepts any mathematically valid pair.
usefulness.benefit: Eliminates false negatives common in rigid exact-match string diff graders.

usefulness.use_case: Memory Bounds & Linear Array Traversal Gating
usefulness.example: Verifies that array indexing does not produce off-by-one errors or out-of-bounds access on negative target numbers.
usefulness.benefit: Guarantees runtime index safety prior to production algorithm deployment.

limitations.example: If a student outputs a different valid index pair than the single reference output, strict line-by-line diffs fail unless a Special Judge is active.
limitations.mitigation: AutoGrader includes an integrated two_sum validator that verifies arr[i] + arr[j] == target dynamically.

limitations.limitation: CPU L1/L2 Cache Locality Skewing Timing Curves
limitations.example: An O(N) linear scan on a small array fits entirely in CPU cache, showing sub-microsecond runtimes that distort empirical curve fitting.
limitations.mitigation: Profile hardware instruction retirement counts and CPU cycles rather than raw wall-clock duration.
